Rest areas at opening stayed on our minds, and we appreciate your feedback. You said the companion rest space felt neglected during boarding and that the handling of your pet's comfort made the trip feel less careful than it should have been. That is useful to hear, because steady animal care depends on clear checks, calm pacing, and consistent crew follow-through.

For routine service, our desk expects crews to confirm that the rest area is ready before passengers arrive, to keep pathways clear, and to watch for signs that a pet needs a quieter spot or a brief pause. When those steps are missed, the experience can feel rushed and unsafe, even if the flight itself is otherwise normal. We are passing your concerns to the welfare coordinator so the review can focus on the handoff between desk guidance and cabin execution.

Please keep in mind that companion travel works best when travelers share any special comfort needs before departure, including sensitivity to noise, preferred placement, or a need for more settling time. That lets the crew use the right instructions from the start and reduces avoidable stress for the animal. We also ask travelers to let staff know right away if a rest area is not being maintained as expected, since a prompt report helps us correct the issue while the journey is still underway.

Aurelia Skyways aims for dependable companion travel, and that means we treat reports like yours as part of safety work, not as routine complaints to file away. We will review the service notes, reinforce the standard with the team, and look for where the care chain slipped. Thank you for taking the time to speak up, because direct feedback helps us improve the experience for people and animals alike. Companion Animal Travel Desk
